mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 typically ranges from £6,500 to £9,000 for supply only, depending on the specialist and the extent of upgrades included. Used engines start around £3,500 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing 448DT engine in a Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 are belt tensioner noise, oil leaks from the heat exchanger or oil pump, or turbo drain pipe issues leading to oil starvation. You should also watch for illuminated temperature warning lights or unusual engine noises.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A typical Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 holds a UK market value of £18,000-£55,000, making a £6,500-£9,000 rebuilt engine a financially sound investment that preserves the vehicle's performance, refinement, and strong resale value for years to come. The 448DT is widely regarded as the most reliable Sport engine.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 typically takes 3 to 5 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the turbo system are being upgraded simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt unit may add a few days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 and the 3.0 SDV6 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 uses a 4.4-litre V8 diesel engine (448DT) producing 313-339 hp, prioritising effortless refinement, genuine V8 character, and superior reliability with no catastrophic bottom-end design flaws. In contrast, the 3.0 SDV6 uses a V6 diesel (306PS) focused on fuel economy but carries the notorious crankshaft snapping weakness.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the L494 Range Rover Sport launched, the 4.4 SDV8 badge represented the diesel flagship - a powerful, refined V8 diesel delivering effortless torque and genuine V8 character, widely considered the most reliable engine in the Sport line-up.

milestones.description: Introduction of the 448DT 4.4L SDV8 V8 diesel engine (313-339 hp, 740 Nm) in the L494 Range Rover Sport, assembled at Ford's Mexican plant and fitted exclusively to high-end variants.
2020 - Continued production with minor refinements; the 448DT maintained its reputation as the most durable Sport engine with no catastrophic bottom-end design flaws.
Discontinuation of the 4.4 SDV8 in the Range Rover Sport due to emissions regulations, replaced by mild-hybrid six-cylinder Ingenium units in the L461 generation.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

However, age-related wear on turbo components, belt systems, and cooling is a known pattern. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: Turbo Drain Pipe & Belt Tensioner Failure
problems.h4: Turbo Drain Pipe & Belt Tensioner Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 448DT Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: Early units suffer from turbo drain pipe defects leading to oil starvation risk, while belt tensioner roller displacement can cause drive belt breakage. Heat exchanger and oil pump leaks are common after 80k miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace belt tensioner, inspect turbo drain pipes, replace heat exchanger seals.
repairOptions.longevity: Extends life significantly if caught before catastrophic failure occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded turbo and belt components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has already suffered oil starvation or belt-related damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 of relevant age (2014-2020) currently holds a UK market value of approximately £18,000-£55,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader market observations]. At this premium value band, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine replacement is a small fraction of the vehicle's worth and easily justifies the investment to preserve performance, refinement, and strong resale value.
problems.recommendation: If your Range Rover Sport 4.4 V8 is showing early signs of belt wear or minor oil leaks but has not suffered catastrophic failure, a preventative belt tensioner and turbo drain pipe refresh by a JLR specialist is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has already suffered oil starvation or belt breakage, a full rebuilt replacement is the only reliable long-term solution.
